item.title: MLIT approves international passenger facility fee caps at Kochi Airport
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-20, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism approved passenger facility fee caps for Kochi Airport Building Co., Ltd. under Article 16 of the Airport Act. The company is a designated airport functional facility operator under Article 15 of that Act. The tax-inclusive caps for international flights are JPY 1,300 for passengers aged 12 or older and JPY 650 for children aged 2 to under 12; the child rate also applies to children under 2 using a child ticket. Collection is scheduled for tickets issued on or after 2027-04-07, with the fee included in the ticket and collected together with the airfare. item.title: MLIT announces review of Keisei Electric Railway's proposed passenger fare-cap changes
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-19, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism announced that the Transport Council had begun reviewing Keisei Electric Railway Co., Ltd.'s application to change railway passenger fare caps, following a ministerial referral dated 2026-11-18. The application proposes average fares paid increasing by 14.1% overall: 14.3% for ordinary fares and 13.7% for season tickets, comprising a 16.9% increase for commuter tickets and an 11.5% decrease for student tickets. These comparisons include the existing railway-station accessibility surcharge, which the application proposes abolishing alongside the fare revision. A public hearing under Article 23 of the Act for Establishment of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism is planned in Tokyo in January 2027, with the exact date, venue and participation procedures to be announced separately. This is an application under review, not an approved fare change; the excerpts do not state an implementation date. item.title: MLIT announcement: RFI on overseas infrastructure project development
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-19, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) announced a request for information (RFI) to inform future commissioning of overseas project-development studies and related work. It requests information on preliminary feasibility-stage studies and Japanese construction methods and technologies, including demonstrations, that could support adoption abroad, government-to-government engagement or public-private business matching. The six themes are infrastructure management, disaster prevention and resilience, smart cities, infrastructure digital transformation, green infrastructure, and urban development, including environmentally conscious development. Covered construction fields include roads, rivers, water supply and sewerage, water resources, erosion control, disaster prevention, cities, housing and construction technology. The stated submission period is 2026-11-19 to 2026-12-09, for companies, industry associations and others with relevant expertise or technologies; follow-up interviews may be conducted. item.title: Cabinet approves commencement and implementing orders for urban renaissance amendments
item.description: AI summary: The implementing Cabinet Order specifies urban facilities, including roads, parks and plazas, covered by the new urban renaissance development agreement system; it also defines exemptions from notification requirements for alterations to specified buildings in designated local-character areas. It additionally sets a minimum land-area requirement for residents and others proposing plans to maintain and enhance historic character, although the excerpt gives neither the threshold nor the detailed exemptions. On 2026-11-17, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism announced Cabinet approval of this order amending related Cabinet Orders and a separate commencement order. The latter sets 2026-11-24 as the commencement date, except for certain provisions, of the Act Partially Amending the Act on Special Measures concerning Urban Renaissance and Other Acts (Act No. 23 of 2026), which was promulgated on 2026-05-27. item.title: MLIT announcement: Project applications for PPP/PFI public-private dialogue
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-13, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) announced project recruitment for online public-private dialogue scheduled for 2027-01-28, to gather private-sector views on public-private partnership/private finance initiative (PPP/PFI) projects. Eligible applicants are public-facility administrators, including local governments and other public bodies, considering project concepts, project implementation or operator selection. The stated application period is 2026-11-13 at 14:00 to 2026-12-04 at 17:00; an application is received only after both the online submission and project registration form are completed.
